title: Attain the sharp three-axis Gaussian grid error with an exact inverse
body:
Three-axis nearest rounding cannot be injective: both zero and a unit input have unique nearest output zero. This package gives an explicit alternative with an exact inverse, exact complex sum, exact fourth power and zero fixed. A permutation of 64 lattice cosets attains uniform error `2h` on eight Gaussian entries. A half-grid input proves that **no integer-output rule can have a smaller uniform error** for this ideal operator.

The construction was pushed beyond its first candidate. A complete 700,833-vector search proves the fixed-coset centre optimum is squared error five. A sum-preserving coset permutation reduces it to four. The same package retains both the scoped centre certificate and the stronger final construction; no separate result is counted for the intermediate candidate.

Whole calls now have certificate `ceil(f/3) h sqrt(N/2)`, compared with `ceil(f/2) h sqrt(N/2)` from PR6534. The group plan minimizes this certificate, then data additions, among groups of sizes one, two and three. Complete two-call and three-call ports return both dirty banks. The runtime table has 3,072 payload bytes. An eight-point block uses 80 additions, 28 negations, eight exchanges and sixteen quarter shifts, plus the explicit classification, table and checking work. No total runtime or physical tariff improvement is claimed.

Evidence: all 64 centre minima, every matching edge, exact matrix identities, 1,024 large signed coset cases, sixteen complete calls through f=4, twelve full ports through f=3 and every grouping through f=128 pass. Normal/optimized registered CPython 3.12, committed bytes/modes, official 22-file export with nine retained inputs, read-only Git-free empty-PATH replay and source-corruption rejection pass. The checkout is shallow; optional full-history validation was not run. Hosted CI and independent scientific acceptance remain separate.

Scope: this is a changed indexed-grid contract. Pointwise nearest output, global phase covariance, ideal-square rewrites, selected-child admission, reversible Boolean/tape pricing, framework-assumption discharge and new kappa are not supplied. The global optimum concerns uniform eight-point grid error, not whole-call error or physical cost.

Reproduce: `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/three-axis-coset-rounding`.

Base: canonical main `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority 8, selected PR6030, refreshed before work and submission. Overlap covered 485 open PRs and 6,473 Discussion records, then live handoffs and recent PRs. Randomized/coarsening work in PR6532 and Discussion1166 remains separate. The canonical claim and update are in Discussion5475.

Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit PR6534 for two-axis fusion; PR6509 for the conservative pair kernel and direct matrix oracle; JoyboyBrian / PR5485 and the retained PR4743 lineage for the complete ports. Exact source bytes, ancestry and origin records are included. Walsh transforms, lattice quotients, closest-vector enumeration and bipartite matching are classical. Apache-2.0.

[Scoped claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5475#discussioncomment-19365648).
